questions.question: Tell me about a PostgreSQL database you were responsible for in production. What did you change in its schema or indexes, and how did you decide?
follow_ups: How did you read the query plan, and what did it show?
What would you do differently now?
listen_for: owned decisions, not just used the database
reasons tied to query patterns or data size
warning_signs: only ever used the database through an ORM someone else configured
can't explain why an index helped

questions.question: Tell me about a schema or data change you shipped on a large production table. How did you avoid downtime and lock problems?
follow_ups: How would you roll it back halfway through?
How did you backfill existing rows?
warning_signs: only ran tool-generated migrations on small or staging data
no idea how long the change locked the table

questions.question: Imagine schema migrations run automatically when each application instance starts, and you run several instances. What can go wrong, and how would you change the process?
follow_ups: How would old and new versions of the app run against the same schema during a rollout?
listen_for: moves migrations to a separate pre-deploy step
warning_signs: proposes stopping all instances for every change

questions.question: A list endpoint gets slower every week as data grows. It counts all rows and pages with OFFSET. How would you investigate and fix it?
follow_ups: How would you prove the fix worked?
warning_signs: jumps to caching or bigger hardware without measuring

questions.question: In an ORM you've used in production, how have you dealt with queries that loaded far more data, or ran far more queries, than expected?
follow_ups: How did you find out it was happening?
warning_signs: treats the ORM as a black box

questions.question: How would you set up tests for database code so that tests can't affect each other, and still run quickly?
follow_ups: How would you test the migrations themselves?
listen_for: containers or a real database in CI
warning_signs: one shared database with cleanup at the end
mocks the database entirely for DB logic

questions.question: What would you put in place first to make a single production PostgreSQL instance reliable, and why that order?
follow_ups: How would you know a backup actually works?
